prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer stands directly to the left of a silver motorcycle (within 0.3–1.0 m), with the wearer's chest and arms at the bottom of the frame (0.2–0.5 m) reaching forward to grasp the right handlebar and brake lever directly beneath a raised side mirror. The side mirror (0.3–0.4 m) and upper windshield fairing (0.4–0.6 m) appear brightest as the nearest elevated surfaces above the handlebars, while the tiled floor below and to the right recedes to roughly 1.5–2.0 m in the dark background. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer's hands and torso remain at a steady distance on the handlebar, while a second person enters from the far right edge in frame 4 and approaches to about 0.8–1.2 m to the right of the wearer and roughly 0.5–0.8 m from the motorcycle's front wheel in frame 5, facing forward parallel to the bike and looking away from the wearer. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the vertical layering of the protruding side mirror, the hands underneath it, the lower motorcycle body, and the floor, though it is unreliable on the translucent windshield in frames 3–4 (overestimating closeness as bright white) and blurs the boundaries of the second person and motion-blurred mirror in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map labels the camera wearer's torso and arms in the lower foreground (0.2–0.5 m) as 'person' and the adjacent vehicle to the upper left and center (0.3–1.2 m away, within arm's reach of both hands) as 'motorcycle' against an unlabelled floor background. Across the 5 frames, the side mirror partially occludes the wearer's left hand and the handlebar assembly, while the bulk of the motorcycle behind the front fairing and the second person's upper body on the right remain out of the field of view. In frame 3, a small 'person' mask at the lower-right edge captures the approaching second person's foot (~1.2 m away to the right) before it becomes obvious in the main workspace, and the map delineates the contour between the wearer's arms and the motorcycle fairing in frames 1, 3, and 4. However, the segmentation is highly unreliable overall: it completely misses the motorcycle in frames 2 and 5, fails to segment the second person standing ~0.8–1.2 m to the right in frames 4 and 5, and fragments the wearer and motorcycle into overlapping, boxy false-positive 'person' masks in frame 3 while misclassifying the side mirror in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, and 5, and only renders a partial body and hand skeleton for the camera wearer in the lower-center foreground (0.2–0.5 m from the camera) in frames 3 and 4. In frames 3 and 4, the yellow torso and arm links show the wearer's shoulders at the bottom of the frame with both arms extending forward and upward toward the motorcycle's right handlebar (roughly 0.4–0.5 m away, within direct reach), where the hands converge and magenta finger keypoints appear on the right hand in frame 4. When combined with the RGB context, these skeletons indicate that the camera wearer is facing forward toward the front of the motorcycle and looking down at the handlebar grip, even where the left hand is partly occluded beneath the black side mirror. While the pose map makes the exact joint angles of the wearer's tucked elbows and overlapping wrists under the mirror easier to trace than in the bulky red jacket of the RGB image, it is unreliable because it misses the wearer entirely in three of the five frames, misplaces head/neck keypoints near the hands due to the top-down egocentric angle, and never detects the second person walking past on the right in frames 3 to 5.
